notes: The Li-Po battery is not in the catalogue, so I added lipo-battery with POS and NEG ports.

The MKR WiFi 1010 catalogue entry has no JST port. The battery-to-board joined and electrical edges therefore leave the board port null. The schematic shows the battery's + and - going to the board's JST connector.
The pushbutton straddles the breadboard centre gap at column 8. I put its legs at 8b.f (the upper half of the picture, rows f-j) and 8t.e (the lower half, rows a-e).
The black GND wire ends in column 8 on the f-j side (8b.g). The yellow pin 8 wire ends in column 8 on the a-e side (8t.d). Both land on the same strips as the button legs, as the picture shows.
The micro-USB power source is mentioned in the text for charging the battery but is not drawn in the circuit images, so I left it out.
The board's GND is the single GND pin of the MKR WiFi 1010.

Validator item V3 (e3 and e5, pin to breadboard-hole), kept on purpose. These are the two joins of the pushbutton legs into breadboard holes, which the circuit image shows. The mismatch comes from the catalogue 'pushbutton' entry giving its ports the kind 'pin'. I kept the catalogue type, as the spec requires, instead of inventing a duplicate button type with lead ports.

Validator item E5 (pin 8 floating when the button is open), kept on purpose. The manual wires the button directly between D8 and GND. No pull resistor appears in the image, the schematic or the parts list, and the text says the button 'goes between D8 and GND'. The sketch uses the board's internal pull-up on the wake-up pin, so pin 8 does not float in the real circuit. An external resistor would be a part the manual does not use.
